headline: High: Cline’s default workspace/file and MCP access can interact badly with a non-runnable content repo, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing repo with no runtime isolation or I/O surfaces, while agent B reads/writes workspace files and can use MCP. If A’s content is placed in B’s workspace, B may treat it as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible in default Cline workflows, but not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF agent A’s repository content is opened in agent B’s workspace
IF agent B parses workspace files as instructions or prompts
IF an MCP server or file bridge exposes A’s content to B
mitigations: Keep agent A content in a read-only folder outside B’s workspace
Disable MCP servers for the session
Use a separate workspace per agent
Add a manual review step before B acts on any file content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad filesystem and network egress, so any sensitive material in a shared workspace could be transmitted outward. Agent A itself shows no data classes touched, but its repository content can still be copied into B’s workspace. The pairwise leakage path is therefore workspace-mediated and credible, though not directly evidenced as sensitive data exposure.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the workspace shared with agent B
IF agent B reads those files before making network calls
IF model-provider or browser actions transmit workspace-derived content
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate non-networked workspace for agent B
Turn off browser and network actions for the session
Store sensitive inputs in a different directory with access controls
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B explicitly supports filesystem writes and shared state via filesystem across instances. Agent A has no runtime capabilities, so direct conflict is limited; however, if A’s repo content is used as a shared artifact, B can overwrite or modify it. Uncertainty about A’s operational surface pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent A’s files are placed in the same directory that agent B writes to
IF multiple B instances operate on the same workspace
IF git state is modified without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory
Avoid concurrent B instances on the same repo
Pause git operations while B is active
Use branch-per-task workflows
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can act on workspace content and browser outputs, so if it consumes A’s material as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into code changes or external actions. Agent A is a prompt-engineering content repo, which increases the chance that B will reuse its text as guidance. The pairwise pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous downstream harm.
conditions: IF B uses A’s content as source material without verification
IF B converts A’s text into code, prompts, or browser actions
IF downstream actions are enabled in B’s session
mitigations: Require B to cite source lines before acting
Review B’s proposed changes before commit
Limit B to read-only mode for analysis tasks
Separate research content from execution workspaces
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool actions

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles model-provider API keys and can send data to external services, while agent A is a public open-source content repo with no sensitive-data profile. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of shared workspace content rather than a clear policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent B’s workspace
IF outbound requests include that regulated data
IF the operator relies on B for data subject or residency-sensitive workflows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B’s workspace
Use redacted samples for testing
Disable outbound network calls when handling sensitive material
Document data-handling boundaries for the session
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
